audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers render different level charts. content win[] (and packet.levelChart) read Orianna/Orianna/Orianna/Orianna/Skill/Skill/Orianna; the full layer reads Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Vladimir/Vladimir. Rows 5 and 6 are opposite verdicts.
audit.why: packet.levelChart and content win[] agree, so the full layer is the outlier. Vladimir is a weak pre-6 laner (600-range Q, health-cost E, no mobility until W at 3) and Orianna out-ranges him at 815, which supports the early Orianna rows; the late row goes to Orianna because Sanguine Pool rescues only Vladimir while Shockwave sets up the whole team.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side -> Orianna, phases[5].side -> Skill (why rewritten to an even first-item window), phases[6].side -> Orianna (why rewritten to the pool-vs-Shockwave asymmetry).

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes listed only owner spikes and never named the anti-heal timing, even though Vladimir's whole spike pattern is sustain.
audit.why: missingInteractions rule 'needs-antiheal': Transfusion (Q, 9s down to 4.6s, 0 cost) and Hemoplague (R, 120s) both heal him, so Grievous Wounds timing decides extended trades. His first-item sustain is what evens the lane at row 5.
audit.corrected: breakdown.spikes now names Oblivion Orb before his second item; phases[5].why states the sustain-vs-poke stalemate.
sources: enemyKit Q and R heal flags

audit.whatIsWrong: Ability names were all correct, but no interaction was actually stated: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit, and the text implied Transfusion costs him resources while attributing the health cost to nothing.
audit.why: Kit: Sanguine Pool 28/25/22/19/16s, 2s untargetable, 350 range. Transfusion 9/7.9/6.8/5.7/4.6s, 0 cost. Tides of Blood is the ability that pays his own health. Orianna E 9s / 1095, R 110/95/80 / 410, Q 815.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt on real numbers (pool 28s->16s and its 2s untargetable window, Transfusion 9s->4.6s, own E 9s); dosFull[0].d now states his 600 range and the health cost sitting on E, not Q.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere; breakdown.cooldowns had no digit in it.
audit.corrected: Sequencing is now explicit: bait the 28s pool, trade inside the Transfusion gap, hold the 110s R for his Hemoplague commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed in dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[2].d; the content 'mid' field contained a garbled fragment ('force his mana... his health-cost sustain').
audit.why: Defect-catalogue item 2, plus a visible broken sentence shipping to a paying reader.
audit.corrected: Bodies rewritten to match their titles; 'mid' repaired to name Tides of Blood's health cost.

edits.before: Luden's spike: Q-W chunks a third of his bar. Shove, rotate, and let the ball-delivery threat run the river fights.
edits.after: Your Luden's meets his first-item sustain: Q-W chunks him, Transfusion heals it back — the row is even until anti-heal.

edits.before: Late Ori is the teamfight: protect-ball on your diver, shockwave their clump, and dissonance the choke they retreat through.
edits.after: Grouped, Shockwave sets up your whole team while Sanguine Pool rescues only him — ball on your frontliner and start the fight.

edits.before: Vladimir wins by landing Sanguine Pool, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Vladimir wins by surviving to two items, healing back every poke with Transfusion, and Hemoplaguing your whole team.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E Command: Protect has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5 — 2s untargetable, long enough to eat your whole combo, so bait it and commit on the downtime. - Transfusion: 9s at rank 1 down to 4.6s — trade in the gap before he heals. - Your E is 9s: shield the Hemoplague tick.

edits.before: Lost Chapter steadies the trade game; level 6 doubles your lane presence; Luden's makes Q-W a third of a health bar.
edits.after: Lost Chapter steadies the trade game; level 6 doubles your presence; buy Oblivion Orb before his second item.

edits.before: Carry through the ball — no champion controls teamfight space like Orianna; one Shockwave on three is a won game, and you decide when it happens.
edits.after: Carry through the ball — Vladimir's pool saves only himself, so a Shockwave that lands on his carries wins the fight he cannot rescue.

edits.before: Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: His Q is 600 range and his E costs health — a ball parked on the melee wave taxes every last-hit he walks to.

edits.before: Vladimir spends Sanguine Pool early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Your passive grows on repeat autos, so weave one after each Q — he has no way to shove you off.

edits.before: That is Vladimir’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Ball idle at 815 leaves you shield-less while he heals back.

edits.before: Poking with the ball stranded at max range when his engage is up — an Orianna without her ball is a Doran's Ring with legs.
edits.after: A 110-second ultimate on minions is the fight you lose later — hold R to answer his Hemoplague commit or to pull him off your carry.

edits.before: Through 4-5 you keep bullying - shove him in, deny CS, and force his mana... his health-cost sustain, so he is always trading HP to farm under your poke. Level 6 flips to even: Hemoplague and Sanguine Pool give him an all-in plus an escape, so keep the pressure but don't dive a fresh pool.
edits.after: Through 4-5 you keep bullying - shove him in, deny CS, and make him pay health for Tides of Blood every time he clears, so he is always trading HP to farm under your poke. Level 6 flips to even: Hemoplague and Sanguine Pool give him an all-in plus an escape, so keep the pressure but don't dive a fresh pool.

notes: diff 'TRICKY' / diffRating 7/10 sits oddly against a 48.87% win rate and a level chart that gives Orianna four of seven rows, but the rating is defensible on Vladimir's scaling (carry threat 7.5/10) so it was left alone rather than guessed at — see questionsForUser. phases[2].why and phases[3].why are Orianna-generic templates that could be pasted onto any enemy; nothing in Vladimir's kit gave a grounded replacement that fit the length band, so they were left. phases[N].rating untouched (polarity of the number is not derivable from the data). Sanguine Pool's interaction with a landed Command: Shockwave (whether the 2s untargetability drops the pending knockup) is not in Riot's text and was not asserted anywhere.
